newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stops army offensive against Moslem rebels.
newsitem.headline: Manila stops army offensive against Moslem rebels.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Tuesday ordered the army to stop all offensives against Moslem rebels to allow the resumption of ceasefire talks with the guerrillas.
"If there is fighting, it's very hard to talk. That's why the order is, don't make any offensive action, stay put," presidential adviser Alexander Aguirre told reporters.
But if government forces were attacked they could retaliate, he said.

The insurgent Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) postponed ceasefire talks scheduled for last month after clashes with government forces in which the military said scores of rebels and 15 soldiers died. Soldiers also overran a major rebel base.
The MILF on Monday threatened to pull out of the talks altogether if the military attacked its main camp where an estimated 6,000 guerrillas were entrenched.
The MILF is fighting for an Islamic state on southern Mindanao island, which Moslems in this largely Christian country regard as their ancestral homeland.
Manila signed a peace deal last year with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) but the MILF was not a party to the accord.
